relevance_note: Single-patient letter describing a woman with Tangier disease and an ABCA1 variant: "Genetic analyses revealed a homozygotic mutation in ABCA1 at the 913 amino acid position".
method_note: Read the whole letter (no tables, no supplement); built the JSON with a short Python script from my own reading and checked every span verbatim against the Markdown. One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5). No HGVS is printed: the variant is described as 'A>T non-sense point mutation ... at nucleotide 2737 in Exon 19' (Figure 2 legend) and as K(AAG) to stop codon (TAG) at amino acid 913 (text); variant_original_string keeps the Markdown's '>' literally; cdna/protein HGVS fields left null and no transcript inferred. Pathogenicity recorded as 'novel' from the figure legend wording. ethnicity_or_country 'Japan' rests on the sentence placing her as the second of 31 Japanese Tangier cases with connective tissue disease; the paper does not state her nationality directly. Age at onset taken from initial presentation with low serum cholesterol at 35 years; no age at diagnosis or at last evaluation is stated ('before the patient turned 60' is a treatment plan, not an evaluation age). Normal ECG, ultrasound cardiogram and carotid ultrasound were recorded as the paper names them (excluded 'abnormal ...'); per narrow-vs-broad, they do not exclude the checklist items coronary artery disease or non-coronary atherosclerotic arterial disease, which stay 'not reported'. 'Extremely low in levels of slow-migrating LDL' is an LDL subfraction, not LDL cholesterol, so 'low LDL cholesterol' stays 'not reported'. References 3 and 8 (Zhang 2007; Uehara 2008, on Tangier disease) are cited but the paper does not state that this patient was described there, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null. Fibromyalgia: the text first says it 'could not be ruled out', then concludes she was 'diagnosed as having not FM'; recorded as excluded from the final statement (not treated as a contradiction).
